newsitem.title: USA: National Fuel to boost E&P outlays.
newsitem.headline: National Fuel to boost E&P outlays.

text.p: National Fuel Gas Co will boost exploration and production spending in 1997, ending September 30, while trimming utility capital spending, spokeswoman Theresa M. Steiner told Reuters Friday.
She said spending is expected to total $206.4 million this year, up from the $171.6 million spent last year and the $182.8 million spent in fiscal 1995.
"We are excited at the future prospects of our exploration and production operations," chief executive Bernard J. Kennedy explained.
He said the company is projecting 1997 capital expenditures for this segment of $116.2 million, compared to $83.6 million last year and $69.7 million in 1995.
"The accomplishments of our offshore drilling program in the Gulf Coast region contributed greatly to the increased earnings for 1996," Kennedy pointed out.
Wednesday the company reported a 38 percent jump in annual profits to a record $104.7 million, or $2.78 per share.
Reporting operating income of $72.9 million from exploration and production, up from 1995's 67.9 million, it said the increase reflects higher production and prices.

Seneca Resources Corp's Gulf Coast program continued to drive this segment's growth. Offshore finds at West Cameron 552 and Vermilion 252 were the major contributors to production increases for the year.
Overall, National Fuel said, production volumes nearly doubled to 49.2 billion cubic feet equivalent from 25.4 billion in 1995. Natural gas production increased 86 percent to 38.8 billion cubic feet.
1995 production was delayed when prices were low to preserve the value of reserves for shareholders, it noted.
Steiner said Pipeline and Storage spending is also budgeted to increase in 1997, to $25.3 million from $22.3 million last year, but remain below 1995's 38.7 million.
Other nonregulated activities spending will follow a similar pattern, she said, rising to $5.4 million from $3.2 million last year, but remaining below 1995's $9.5 million.
National Fuel said its other nonregulated operations experienced a loss last year compared to 1995 mainly because of expenses associated with developing international opportunities.

In August, it said, Horizon Energy Development Inc withdrew from participation in the development of a 151 megawatt power plant near Kabirwala, Punjab Province, in east-central Pakistan. As a result, about $5.9 million or $0.16 per share was charged to earnings.
As a partial offset, National Fuel Resources, the company's marketing subsidiary, reported stronger earnings on increased volumes and improved margins, the company said.
Steiner said spending on utility operations is expected to decline to $59.6 million from $63.7 million in 1996 and $64.8 million in 1995. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
